correctness.rationale: The PBH eigenspace decomposition is exact for K_m square K_n; top eigenmodes coincide with alternating cycle flows, yielding forest iff. For m!=n any surviving middle mode would force two fully unselected rows or columns and a forbidden 4-cycle. For m=n, the eigenspace collision yields component potentials with exactly two independent weighted-sum equations; the 2-vector component rank is necessary and sufficient. An exact tree complement count subtracts only n^2 double-stars and n^2(n-1)^2 one-selected-edge components for n>=3; the 2x2 case is checked separately. Independently constructed integer PBH ranks and combinatorial tests agree on all subsets of five boards and all 11,440 4x4 minimum candidates. Finite verification is not claimed as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus semantic searches and accessible prior-claim comparisons yielded no equivalent or stronger theorem. The relevant full-text published sources treat zero forcing as sufficient, Cartesian products of paths, or general control complexity; the product-graph paper available abstract explicitly studies one binary input b rather than the independent input matrix B_S. The closest previously catalogued findings concern the different subdivision graph with added original-state vertices and line graphs of multipartite graphs with at least three parts, so neither implies the rook-graph forest plus equal-side resonance classification. An unindexed specialist result and the inaccessible 2020 full manuscript remain documented risks, but are not decisive contrary evidence.

value.rationale: The rook graph is the canonical line graph of K_m,n and a Cartesian product of complete graphs, so independently actuated coordinate controllability is a natural graph-control design question. The exact all-set forest plus resonance test replaces repeated eigenvector rank computations, detects a genuine equal-factor collision that removes n^2((n-1)^2+1) spanning-tree placements, and gives exact actuator minimum and labeled placement counts for all m,n>=2. Neither a mechanical graph renaming nor a known-table recomputation; the square correction is mathematically motivated and nontrivial.
